..
Issued at 411 PM CDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Currently through tonight...

Was a dreary start to the day today across the area, with
plentiful low-level stratus, and even some drizzle/foggy 
conditions across mainly WNW portions. The fog diminished 
largely by mid-morning...the stratus a bit more stubborn, with a
couple of lingering stripes across central and SErn portions 
keeping skies partly-mostly cloudy...elsewhere is plenty of sun.
Looking aloft, seeing generally west-southwesterly flow in 
place...set up between broad ridging along the East Coast and 
broad troughing over the western CONUS...with satellite imagery 
showing an embedded shortwave trough working its way east across
the Dakotas/Central Plains. The accompanying surface cold front
continues to push southeast across the area...here at mid-
afternoon has worked its way through roughly have of the 
forecast area. The timing of this front and lingering cloud 
cover has resulted in quite a temp gradient across the 
area...with mid-60s across the NNWrn half and near 80 in the far
SE corner.

The rest of this afternoon into tonight...this front will
continue sinking south, with models showing it stalling as it 
moves into central KS, losing its upper level push. There may be
a brief period closer to 00Z were isolated precip could develop
along the front, potentially clipping far SE portions of mainly
Mitchell County...but models keep the better chances just off 
to our SE. Expecting overall quiet conditions through the rest 
of this evening/overnight...and not out of the question there 
could be patchy fog again early Thursday AM.

Thursday through this weekend....

During the daytime hours on Thursday, much of the forecast area
is still looking to see dry conditions. Models showing 
shortwave upper level ridging pushing across the region...ahead 
of a disturbance that will be working its way NNE out of Mexico 
into the TX/NM border region. Late in the afternoon, not out of 
the question some isolated precipitation could develop across 
far SSWrn portions of the forecast area...but better chances 
look to hold off until the evening/overnight hours, spreading 
across the rest of the forecast area as the low-level jet/WAA 
increases. Instability remains in the area, keeping the 
potential for thunderstorms in the forecast...but the overall 
threat for severe weather remains low. 

As we get into the daytime hours on Friday...precip from the 
overnight hours should wane/shift off to the east, leaving a 
relative lull in activity, before the next round moves in. Just
how long of a lull this ends up being still has some 
uncertainties...models at 00Z Saturday showing the main upper 
level disturbance is just off to our SSW. Thinking is at least 
scattered activity will be working its way into southern 
portions of the forecast area...some models hint at it being 
well into our Neb. counties by 00Z as well. Some details still 
to be ironed out. The overall best/widespread chances are still 
focused in the 00Z-12Z Saturday time frame. Threat for 
thunderstorms also remains, but again the overall threat for 
severe weather is low...the forecast area remains just in the 
General Thunderstorm area for both the SPC Days 2 and 3 
outlooks.

The main upper level disturbance continues to work its way
across the Central Plains on Saturday...and preciptiation 
chances look to be waning with time from west to east. 
Confidence in the exact timing of when precip comes to an end is
not high, forecast chances are only 20 percent by late in the 
day Saturday/Sat evening. The daytime hours on Sunday look to 
mainly be quiet.

As far as temperatures go through the end of the week-
weekend...highs for Thu-Fri looking to range from the low 60s NW
to low 70s SE, with the weekend mainly in the low-mid 60s. 

Early next week...

Models continuing to show the potential for a larger, stronger
upper level system to work its way through the western CONUS 
during the upcoming weekend....driving precipitation chances as 
we get into Sunday night on through the start of the new work 
week. Larger scale models still showing plenty of differences 
with the finer details of the troughing through the Rockies and 
the evolution of the deeper upper level low that looks to 
develop over the Plains. Some hint at more of a single, main low
trekking through the heart of the Central Plains...others 
showing flow/energy may end up more split. Either way results in
pretty low confidence as far as precipitation chance/amount 
details go. A more organized low, depending on its 
track/location of the main deformation zone, could bring a 
notable focused swath of rainfall (at least a couple inches not 
out of the question)...a more split pattern could bring more 
scattered, potentially lower amounts. Something to keep an eye 
on in the coming days for anyone with outdoor activities early 
next week.
